question.text: Sahyadri Buyout Fund II (Cat II, corpus INR 1200 crore) has a 10-year tenure with a 5-year commitment period. Per common industry practice described in the chapter, how is the management fee typically structured?

answer.text: Fixed INR 20 crore per annum flat for the entire fund life, regardless of drawdowns
A % of exit proceeds only; no periodic management fee
A % of hurdle rate achievement, with zero fixed fee
1-2.5% per annum of CAPITAL COMMITTED during the commitment period; thereafter reducing to a % of actual INVESTED capital or % of AUM of the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: management fee usually ranges between 1% and 2.5% per annum of CAPITAL COMMITTED during the commitment period. Thereafter, it reduces to a fixed percentage of actual INVESTED capital (if lesser than committed) OR as a percentage of the underlying AUM. The fee can also be on a slab-rate system where the % reduces as commitment size increases. GST is charged over and above the stated fee. The Trap: The flat-INR option replaces the % structure with an unrealistic absolute figure. The exit-proceeds option confuses management fee with performance fee. The hurdle-rate option combines fee with hurdle (which is a carry concept, not a fee concept). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same fee mechanics. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests LP-facing fee disclosures. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) tests PMS fee structures (similar commit-vs-invested distinction for discretionary PMS). Manager's Pro-Tip: In competitive LP processes, consider a STEP-DOWN: 2% on committed during investment period, then 1.5% on invested (remaining) during harvest period. This improves LP IRR at the tail and is a key negotiation lever for anchor LPs.
